findings.summary: A routine pull request can modify the candidate-side executable that decides whether that same pull request is routine-eligible.
evidence: Verification: `.github/workflows/coherence.yml:287-312` checks out the candidate and executes its `scripts/check-claim-generation.py`, while the trusted-base input is used only to load `.fsgg/routine-development.json`.

Verification: `.fsgg/routine-development.json:19-24` does not protect `scripts/check-claim-generation.py` or `.github/workflows/coherence.yml`, and `scripts/check-claim-generation.py:642-650` consults only the changed-path list interpreted by that candidate-side program.

Verification: an isolated direct evaluation of `evaluate_routine` at 2960f09657b4694ded7f3fb5bc4b0021974672bb, with exact marker/head and the changed path `scripts/check-claim-generation.py`, returned `(None, 'routine delivery admitted ...')`; the same result occurred for `.github/workflows/coherence.yml`.
resolution_evidence: Verification: repair head 2fe3e653049310e9197f9b8a7b350ea0606a78c3 makes `.github/workflows/coherence.yml:309-316` extract and run the Python gate from `BASE_SHA`, and the expanded fixture passes a base-gate inversion, but the enclosing workflow remains candidate-controlled on `pull_request`.

Verification: `gh api repos/FS-GG/.github/branches/main/protection` lists `claim-generation` as a required status context, while `gh api repos/FS-GG/.github/rulesets --paginate` returns only the active tag ruleset `release-tags-are-immutable`; no required-workflow or protected-path ruleset provides an authority boundary outside this editable workflow.

Verification: GitHub documents that a `pull_request` workflow uses the PR merge branch and the workflow version present in the event-associated SHA/ref (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflows and https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request). A routine candidate can therefore replace `.github/workflows/coherence.yml` itself, preserve a green job named `claim-generation`, and bypass the base-gate extraction. Repair remains required at a base/organization-trusted required-workflow or path-restriction boundary.

findings.summary: Protected-operation refusal relies on a claimant-supplied operation label and an incomplete protected-path list, so publication automation can be admitted as a source change.
evidence: Verification: `.fsgg/routine-development.json:6-24` allows `source-change`, rejects a marker that declares `publish`, but protects only `.fsgg/`, three workflow-name prefixes, and `registry/`.

Verification: `.github/workflows/kit-auto-publish.yml` and `scripts/kit-auto-publish.py` are publication surfaces whose paths do not match any configured protected prefix; isolated direct evaluations of `evaluate_routine` with either changed path and `operation=source-change` returned routine admission.

Verification: `tests/claim-generation/run.sh:243-259` tests a marker that truthfully declares `publish` and one `.fsgg/` path, but has no negative leg for a protected effect mislabeled `source-change` or for the repository's unlisted publication/authority surfaces.
resolution_evidence: Verification: `.fsgg/routine-development.json:19-32` at 2fe3e653049310e9197f9b8a7b350ea0606a78c3 expands the base-loaded protected set to `.github/`, both roadmap-skill roots, `eng/`, `registry/`, `scripts/`, Coordination authority source, and build/tool configuration surfaces.

Verification: `tests/claim-generation/run.sh:263-292` now inverts candidate mutations of the gate, coherence workflow, kit publisher workflow/script, dispatch broker, and Coordination CLI; independent `tests/claim-generation/run.sh` execution passed 58/58. The remaining enclosing-workflow authority defect is retained separately as R0-CRIT-001.
